title: Hide "Open in file manager" action for blank CD/DVD/BD
line: Blank CDs, DVDs and Blu-rays in Disks & Devices no longer show an Open in File Manager button that only opened the home folder.
explanation: Every device row in Disks & Devices gets its default button from MountAndOpenAction, which is always valid. A blank disc has no file system (no StorageAccess), so the button reads Open in File Manager and runs kde-open with an empty path, which opens the home folder. The change makes MountAndOpenAction invalid for blank optical discs (Solid OpticalDisc::isBlank), exposes that as ActionsInfo.defaultActionValid, and DeviceItem.qml only shows the default button when it is valid; the disc's other actions (e.g. K3b's) stay in the expanded list.

commits.message:
applets/devicenotifier: don't offer Open in File Manager for blank discs

A blank CD, DVD or Blu-ray has no file system, so its Open in File Manager
button could only open the home folder. Make the default action invalid
for blank optical discs and hide the button when it isn't valid.

BUG: 469704

media.caption: Blank CD-RW on master: the row offers Open in File Manager
With the fix: no default button for the blank disc
Expanded on master: K3b action plus the useless Open in File Manager
Expanded with the fix: only the K3b action

reviews.text: This fixes the bug at the right layer across MountAndOpenAction, ActionsInfo, and DeviceItem.qml by marking MountAndOpenAction invalid for blank optical discs without StorageAccess and hiding the default action button when it is invalid. Blank discs no longer show the broken Open in File Manager action that only opened Home, while other disc actions such as K3b remain available in the expanded list and data discs and Audio CDs retain their normal behavior. The patch is minimal, consistent with the existing architecture, and clearly verified.
